summary: King County, WA DNR wooden tower built 1964 as a replacement; used only for emergencies in the 1970s and collapsed in 2008; a 2016 visit found the site being readied for a communication tower.

facts.design: Wooden DNR tower with a live-in cab, metal roof and surround catwalk; height reported as 50, 60 or 70 feet
facts.status_note: Collapsed in 2008; a 2016 visit found the site being prepared for a communication tower, and no source describes lookout remains there now
facts.agency: Washington Dept. of Natural Resources built it; the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register lists 'Washington Dept. of Natural Resources/Weyerhaeuser' as administrator

access.note: A locked gate (#31) closes the road; Willhite Web says permit holders can drive to the site. Sources say the lookout stood on private land.

events.note: Built by the DNR in 1964; Willhite Web quotes a 1964 DNR report calling it a replacement tower
Linda Hill recorded as the lookout (Willhite Web)
Diana Justice recorded as the lookout (Willhite Web)
Forest Fire Lookout Association visit judged the tower legs unsafe because of wood rot within the vertical splice plates
Landowner timber company asked the DNR whether it wanted the tower; the Willhite Web author, then with the DNR, let the offer slip
Tower collapsed. Willhite Web: a Hancock Forestry guard saw it from a distance in mid-July, then found it down a few days later after the snow melted. Register: collapsed under a snow load
Site being prepared for a communication tower; lookout remnants planned for removal (Willhite Web visit)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says 50 feet; the 2008 chapter report says 60 feet; the Register and Willhite Web say 70 feet. No height_m is recorded because the sources do not agree.

The Register lists Washington DNR and Weyerhaeuser as administrator. Willhite Web describes a timber company landowner in 2006 and a Hancock Forestry guard in 2008. The sources do not reconcile these.
The Register says it collapsed under a snow load; Willhite Web offers wind, snow, rot or a mix. Both are reported.

corrections.proposed: Wooden DNR tower with a live-in cab and catwalk; height reported as 50, 60 or 70 feet
corrections.why: The 60-foot figure comes from one source (the 2008 chapter report). The Register and Willhite Web say 70 feet, and firelookout.com says 50.

notes_for_editor: Four sources agree on the 1964 build and the 2008 collapse. Heights (50/60/70 ft) and the landowner name conflict. The only source on the site after 2008 is Willhite Web's 2016 note, and its photo dates are not given, so the 'today' paragraph says we found no current source. Read the Willhite page twice to reach the 2016 passage; no WebSearch used. The washingtonlookouts.weebly.com page was not used for citations.
